question: How does GPT-2-small mechanistically implement indirect object identification (IOI)?
hypothesis: GPT-2-small implements IOI through an attention-head circuit that, at the END position, attends from the prediction site to the indirect-object name token and copies its embedding into the residual stream, raising its logit above competing name candidates. The circuit likely involves earlier-layer components that identify the duplicated subject name and write a signal that biases later attention toward the non-duplicated (indirect-object) name. Specific layer and head identities, and the number of components involved, are unknown a priori and should be discovered empirically by the feature_discovery sub-agent and confirmed by activation patching from corrupted runs.

behavior.description: Given an IOI prompt of the form 'When [A] and [B] went to the [place], [B] gave a [object] to', the model assigns higher logit to the indirect-object name (A) than to the subject name (B) at the final-token prediction position. Holds across both ABBA and BABA template orderings.

dataset.notes: Same as rev1 / Fadi's IOI smoke spec. 500 dev + 100 heldout, ABBA/BABA balanced, single-token names, length-aligned for clean/corrupt pairs. Heldout uses disjoint name pairs from dev.

stages.notes:
Confirm GPT-2-small has a strong IOI signal on the dev split before paying for the discovery loop. logit_diff requires SCALAR target_logits / foil_logits per example — extract logits[last_position, IO_token_id] / logits[last_position, S_token_id] only; do NOT pass full vocab arrays. Abort if accuracy < 0.9.

STAGE DISCIPLINE: this is stage 0 of 6. After committing this stage's metrics and evaluating behavioral-sanity, IMMEDIATELY call advance_stage(). Do NOT write a wrap-up summary — there are 5 stages left.

Two-step pattern:

(A) Discovery sub-agent — call discover_features() once. The sub-agent iterates algorithm_v{N}.py candidates that score attention heads against IOI pairs, and returns a list of top-K candidate (layer, head) sites. Cap inner iterations to ~4. The sub-agent's harness emits per-algorithm patch_effect_recovery numbers in its leaderboard — DO NOT commit those as the criterion's metric. They are PER-ALGORITHM single-head numbers (~0.15 typical), not joint top-K.

(B) Joint top-K patch on dev — after step (A) returns, the master agent extracts the top-K (layer, head) sites from best_summary['top_features'] and runs a JOINT simultaneous patch:

```python
from autointerp.tools.head_patching import HeadPatch, cache_head_z, run_with_head_patches, logit_diff
top_K = [(f['layer'], f['idx']) for f in result['best_summary']['top_features'][:K]]  # K=3 typical
clean_z = cache_head_z(handle, clean_prompts, layers=sorted({L for (L,H) in top_K}))
patches = [HeadPatch(layer=L, head=H, source=clean_z[L][:,:,H,:]) for (L,H) in top_K]
patched_logits = run_with_head_patches(handle, corrupt_prompts, patches, return_logits_at=-1)
joint_lD = logit_diff(patched_logits, IO_token_ids, S_token_ids).mean().item()
recovery = (joint_lD - corrupt_lD) / (clean_lD - corrupt_lD)
```

Commit `recovery` (the JOINT scalar from step B) as patch_effect_recovery's `patched_metric`. The discovery-recovery criterion threshold (0.4) is calibrated for this joint number, not for per-algorithm sub-agent output. Also commit the K (layer, head) sites as CandidateSite artifacts for downstream stages.

If discover_features fails (sub-agent error / SDK issue), fall back to running head_patch_sweep directly (other tools listed: activation_patching) and identify top-K from the per-head matrix, then do the same joint patch in step B. Either path satisfies this stage.

STAGE DISCIPLINE: this is stage 1 of 6. After committing patch_effect_recovery and evaluating discovery-recovery, IMMEDIATELY call advance_stage(). Do NOT write a wrap-up summary — there are 4 stages left.

Validate the discovery output with an exhaustive head_patch_sweep across all 144 (layer, head) pairs, then JOINT top-K. Same recipe as rev3 of the parent IOI spec's localization stage: per-head sweep to RANK, joint patch on top-K to FEED the criterion. Compare the localization top-K with the discovery top-K; if they agree, the discovery sub-agent has surfaced the right circuit. Record agreement/divergence in INVESTIGATION_LOG.md.

STAGE DISCIPLINE: this is stage 2 of 6. After committing kl_to_clean and patch_effect_recovery and evaluating localization-recovery, IMMEDIATELY call advance_stage(). Do NOT write a wrap-up summary — there are 3 stages left (activation_analysis, intervention, validation).

Extract contrastive directions (IO vs S) from the residual stream at candidate layers identified in localization. Mean-ablate the top candidate heads from localization individually and measure ablation_drop on logit_diff. ablation_drop expects (baseline_metric, ablated_metric) scalars.

STAGE DISCIPLINE: this is stage 3 of 6. After committing this stage's metrics, IMMEDIATELY call advance_stage(). Do NOT write a wrap-up summary — there are 2 stages left (intervention, validation).

Path patching from candidate sender heads to the unembed to confirm direct information flow. Build a candidate IOI circuit C (typically the top-3 heads from localization). Measure circuit faithfulness on dev with the SAME END-ONLY ablation methodology validation will use on heldout — see validation stage notes for the worked recipe. faithfulness = (circuit_only - corrupt) / (clean - corrupt). DO NOT mean-ablate complement at all positions; that drives faithfulness negative on GPT-2-small.

AFTER committing this stage's metrics, IMMEDIATELY call advance_stage() to enter the validation stage. Do NOT write a wrap-up summary at this point — the run continues to stage 5.

Evaluate the final circuit C on the HELDOUT split (disjoint names from dev).

CRITICAL: faithfulness uses END-ONLY complement ablation. Worked recipe:

```python
from autointerp.tools.head_patching import HeadPatch, cache_head_z, mean_head_z, run_with_head_patches, logit_diff

clean_cache = cache_head_z(handle, clean_heldout_prompts)
mean_z = mean_head_z(clean_cache)
circuit_set = set(C)  # e.g. [(9,9), (9,6), (10,0)]
patches = []
for L in range(handle.n_layers):
    for H in range(handle.n_heads):
        if (L, H) not in circuit_set:
            patches.append(HeadPatch(layer=L, head=H, source=mean_z[L][:, H, :], positions=[-1]))
circuit_logits = run_with_head_patches(handle, clean_heldout_prompts, patches, return_logits_at=-1)
circuit_lD = logit_diff(circuit_logits, IO_token_ids, S_token_ids).mean().item()
faithfulness_value = (circuit_lD - corrupt_lD) / (clean_lD - corrupt_lD)
```

For minimality: re-run faithfulness with each single component REMOVED from C (so the patches list ALSO ablates the removed head at END). minimality = min(faithfulness_full - faithfulness_minus_one[i]).

minimality's required inputs are (full_circuit_faithfulness: float, removed_faithfulness: list[float] of length len(C)).

This is the FINAL stage. Once both heldout MetricResults (faithfulness, minimality) are committed and both heldout criteria are evaluated, call advance_stage() to terminate the run as COMPLETED. Only AFTER terminal_state == COMPLETED is it appropriate to write a wrap-up summary.

success_criteria.description: GPT-2-small correctly prefers IO over S (logit_diff > 0) on at least 95% of dev samples.

Patching the top-K (typically K=3) attention heads surfaced by the discovery sub-agent JOINTLY into the corrupted run (all K patched simultaneously in ONE forward pass via run_with_head_patches) recovers at least 0.4 of the clean-corrupt logit_diff gap on dev. This is the JOINT recovery scalar from a fresh patch on dev pairs — NOT the sub-agent's per-algorithm patch_effect_recovery from its inner harness's leaderboard. The 0.4 threshold is intentionally lower than localization-recovery's 0.85: discovery is a search step over a small benchmark (n_pairs=30), localization is a full-dev validation. See feature_discovery stage notes for the exact code recipe.

Patching the top-K attention heads identified by exhaustive head_patch_sweep JOINTLY into the corrupted run recovers at least 0.85 of the clean-corrupt logit_diff gap on dev. JOINT recovery scalar (one forward pass with all K HeadPatch entries applied), NOT per-head max from head_patch_sweep['recovery'].max(). See localization stage notes (and rev2 of the parent IOI spec) for the recipe.

Candidate IOI circuit (the K heads selected at localization) achieves faithfulness >= 0.85 on the heldout split. Faithfulness = (circuit_only - corrupt) / (clean - corrupt). The circuit_only forward pass mean-ablates the COMPLEMENT of C ONLY at the END (prediction) position. See validation stage notes for the worked code (HeadPatch with positions=[-1]). Heldout uses disjoint names from dev.

Every head in the final circuit causes a faithfulness drop >= 0.05 when removed (minimality). min(faithfulness_full - faithfulness_minus_one[i]) across the K circuit components must meet the threshold.

abort_if: Stage 1 accuracy < 0.9 — GPT-2-small must be near-ceiling on IOI before discovery makes sense.
Clean-corrupt logit_diff gap < 2.0 nats — contrastive signal too weak for meaningful patching.
risks: Discovery sub-agent's harness may emit per-algorithm patch_effect_recovery scalars (~0.1-0.2) — do not confuse these with the joint top-K recovery the criterion wants.
Sub-agent reward is a moving target if the dev split is small — use the heldout split for the final faithfulness criterion (already enforced by on_split=heldout).
Sub-agent iteration cost can blow the run budget. Cap discover_features max_iterations and watch tool_calls in get_budget.
